units.text: New Apple CEO John Ternus has told staff that most US divisions will get the whole of Thanksgiving week off in recognition of their hard work.

It's oddly hard to confirm this, but some accounts say that Steve Jobs gave staff paid Thanksgiving leave at least once during his time as CEO. But what's certain is that Tim Cook did so for the very first Thanksgiving after he became CEO in 2011.

Now in an email to staff seen by Bloomberg, John Ternus has announced that the tradition will continue. Specifically, alongside the regular Thursday and Friday that firms have, Apple is giving staff Monday to Friday instead:
Team,

Last week in New York, I had the chance to see customers discover for themselves what we already know: Our newest products are incredible! From the most advanced camera ever in an iPhone to intelligent health features in Apple Watch to the amazing listening experience of our latest Air Pods, it was so wonderful to see the joy in people's faces as they experienced our new lineup for the very first time. And that's before iPhone Duo even hits the shelves.

It takes an extraordinary amount of work to make moments like this possible. It takes teams across Apple all driving toward the same goal, every single day. This year has been filled with remarkable milestones, and for all your hard work, you deserve a break.

In recognition of your contributions, most US teams will get the Monday through Wednesday before Thanksgiving off. If you're part of our Retail and AppleCare teams who serve our customers, or international teams, you'll be able to take three extra days off at a later date. You can find all the details on the People site.

I'm so grateful for this amazing team, and I hope you'll use this time away to unwind, recharge, and spend time with loved ones. As I've said, this is an incredibly exciting time to be at Apple. And I can't wait for what's next.
Thanks, John
Once anything like this is established in a large corporation, staff do come to expect it so they won't have been surprised by the news. But they may well have been relieved.
That's because there have been efforts to stop the tradition. There was even pressure on Tim Cook to keep retail stores open on Thanksgiving itself.

The logic there was that it would potentially mean a hugely profitable day for Apple Stores, and in the early 2010s multiple US retailers stayed open. For Macys, Walmart, Sears, and more, opening their stores meant benefiting from the holiday sales rush that normally starts on the following Black Friday.
Apple even tried this in 2012 with the Fifth Avenue store, Hawaii's one on Waikiki Beach, and a Las Vegas store opened. For 2013, more were initially planned to open, but Tim Cook vetoed the plan.

units.text: Apple must pay $5.7 billion for infringing on patents held by Taction Technology, a US jury ruled on Friday. The patents relate to Apple’s Taptic Engine, which is the hardware Apple uses to provide haptic feedback for notifications, button presses, and other interactions.
Taction first filed the lawsuit in 2021, alleging Apple had “infringed and continues to infringe, directly and indirectly” its patents.
As reported by CNBC, the lawsuit centered around two patents:
U.S. Patent No. 10,659,885
U.S. Patent No. 10,820,117

Both patents are focused on a “vibration module for applying vibrational tractions to a wearer’s skin.” Taction argued that Apple’s Taptic Engine infringes upon its patents, saying that Apple was “capitalizing on Taction’s innovation and success.”
Apple’s Taptic Engine first debuted as part of the Apple Watch in 2014 and came to the iPhone 6s and iPhone 6s Plus the following year, replacing the older vibration motor.
In a statement, an Apple spokesperson said:
“While we thank the jury for their consideration, we strongly disagree with today’s verdict and the damages awarded, which are entirely unsupported by the facts.

Apple’s Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction’s technology, which Taction’s own testing of Apple’s products confirmed during trial. Apple does not use Taction’s technology, and we will appeal.”

Taction Technology is a California-based company that describes itself as being “obsessed by sound.” The company says that its “Transporter Technology powers the game-changing Corsair HS60 Haptic headphones, and will soon be powering other premium headphones from major manufacturers.”
In a statement to CNBC, Taction’s lead counsel said:
“We’re happy the jury found for Taction and vindicated its patent rights. Taction waited five and a half years for this case to get to trial, so it was a long time coming.”
You can read the original complaint for patent infringement filed by Taction here and Friday’s jury ruling here.

evidence.discovery_lead: 快科技9月28日消息， 苹果最新推出的A20 Pro芯片正在刷新外界对智能手机性能的认知。最新测试结果显示，搭载A20 Pro的iPhone 18 Pro Max已能通过模拟运行经典开放世界游戏《侠盗猎车手5》，并在接近桌面级显卡NVIDIA GTX 1650的性能水平下流畅运行。 此次测试由开发者项目Vapor完成。虽然《GTA 5》尚未正式推出iOS版本，但开发团队已成功让游戏在iPhone 18 Pro Max上运行，并公开展示完整基准测试数据。 测试结果显示，在1080P分辨率和DirectX 11环境下，游戏在城市驾驶场景中的平均帧率达到66FPS，其他测试场景平均帧率达到80FPS。 为保证画质与性能平衡，测试采用高纹理质量、FXAA抗锯齿、16倍各向异性过滤、75%人口密度、50%视距缩放及锐利阴影设定，同时关闭MSAA抗锯齿。 在这些参数下， A20 Pro运行《GTA 5》的效果已接近GTX 1650显卡在类似设置下的表现。 考虑到这是一颗手机处理器，且游戏仍运行在模拟环境中，这一成绩被认为极具突破性。 测试数据显示， A20 Pro在实现接近GTX 1650游戏性能的同时，性能功耗比达到后者的约11.8倍，即约1180%的优势。这意味着苹果最新移动芯片能以远低于传统桌面显卡的能耗完成相近图形计算任务。 开发者表示，目前《GTA 5》在iPhone上的运行仍属持续开发阶段，一些兼容性问题和视觉细节尚未完全解决，因此当前成绩并非最终版本表现。但即便如此，测试结果已证明现代手机SoC正逐渐进入过去只有PC硬件才能达到的性能领域。 业内人士认为，苹果近年来持续强化移动端3A游戏能力，是实现这一成绩的重要基础。从A17 Pro率先支持主机级游戏，到如今A20 Pro运行大型PC游戏，苹果正不断推动手机游戏平台向高端化发展。 A20 Pro此次取得如此成绩，与苹果采用的新一代芯片封装技术密切相关。 苹果首次在2纳米旗舰处理器上引入WMCM封装方案，将内存颗粒从芯片顶部移至侧面布局，为处理器释放更多散热空间。 同时，iPhone 18 Pro和iPhone 18 Pro Max配备尺寸更大的均热板散热系统，使A20 Pro能在更长时间内维持高性能输出，而不会过早遭遇温度墙限制。 分析人士指出，几年前几乎没人会相信一部智能手机能以接近GTX 1650的性能运行《GTA 5》这样的大型开放世界游戏。而如今，随着2纳米工艺、先进封装技术和移动GPU架构持续进步，手机平台正逐步具备真正运行3A级游戏的能力。 对于整个移动行业而言，A20 Pro的表现不仅意味着苹果芯片实力进一步提升，也反映出智能手机正逐渐演变为一类能够承担轻量级PC娱乐任务的新型计算平台。

units.text: If you’re rocking an iPhone 16 or newer, you might be interested in a Qi2.2 charger to take full advantage of the 25W MagSafe charging speeds that your phone can support. Anker’s new 25W Prime MagSafe 3-in-1 is one of many great options, and it comes in an excellent portable design.
Impressions

The big trend of the latter half of 2025 was bringing 25W Qi2.2 to every single wireless charging accessory possible, and that’s continued through 2026. Anker is kicking things off with a new portable MagSafe 3-in-1 that packs 25W Qi2.2 support into a very portable design.
With 25W of wireless charging, active cooling is practically a necessity. Nearly every 25W charger on the market integrates it, and the new Anker foldable 3-in-1 is no exception.

In the box, you get a 45W charge brick and USB-C cable – providing ample power to charge your iPhone, AirPods, and Apple Watch all at once. With this stand, you can charge an iPhone 18 Pro to 50% in just 27 minutes.

Remember MagSafe Duo? If you were someone who really enjoyed that product before Apple killed it off, you’ll likely enjoy this one. It has extremely similar portability characteristics, but comes with two key benefits: it can serve as a stand, and it can charge three devices at once instead of two.

One neat (though totally unnecessary) feature on this charger is that the Apple Watch charger is spring-loaded. It does fold inwards while you have the charger compacted, but when you’re ready to unfold everything, you just need to press downward on it and it springs outward. I thought that was pretty neat, and helps justify the premium price tag that this product demands.
Wrap up

All in all, if you want a nice MagSafe 3-in-1 charger that can easily work for travel, this new Anker offering is a great choice. Since it includes active cooling, it actually charges your iPhone rather quickly without any of the overheating or other negative side affects that wireless charging can sometimes have.
Anker’s new 3-in-1 MagSafe is available on Amazon with Prime delivery for just $99 currently, in both colors: black and white.

units.text: Apple is, once again, forecast to bring out Apple Glass by the end of 2027, while it also works on a brand new headset that takes after the new Meta VR Glasses.

So far, Apple's head-mounted computing efforts have consisted of the Apple Vision Pro and accessing Siri through AirPods. However, you're still going to have a long wait before being able to try the ever-rumored smart glasses Apple has been persistently working on.

In Sunday's "Power On" newsletter for Bloomberg, Mark Gurman discusses the new Meta VR Glasses and Apple's adjacent work on smart glasses, including Apple Glass. That is, alongside other concepts like AirPods with camera sensors and a new screen-free fitness band.
For the smart glasses, Gurman warns that Apple has a goal of releasing it in some form by the end of 2027.

This reiterates a frequently-raised timeframe for the smart glasses. In September 2025, Gurman said Apple Glass without AR was expected in late 2026 or early 2027, while analyst Ming-Chi Kuo forecast a late 2027 shipping schedule back in June 2025.
Earlier in 2026, a May Gurman newsletter changed expectations for the eyewear to a late 2027 launch.

Current speculation for Apple's glasses is for a first release similar to Meta's Ray-Ban partnership, being glasses with audio, camera, and smart capabilities but without a display for video feedback. A later release would introduce the display element.
More Apple Visions
Gurman's newsletter also mentioned about the woes of the Apple Vision Pro, and touched upon its future plans. This included the Apple Vision team working on a "completely revamped headset."

Referred to as codename N224, it apparently involves engineers exploring four concepts for the headset. This includes offloading some of the internal components from the headset to another component, possibly like a puck.

However, seemingly burned by the tethered battery concept in the Apple Vision Pro, some senior staff at Apple consider this to be a poor user experience. An all-in-one design is more preferable, but doing so while being cheaper and lighter is going to be an engineering challenge.
There's no guarantee of it launching, with the project apparently on "life support." If it does get a release, Gurman speculates a launch in late 2028 or early 2029.

It is a bit for me too, on a personal note. After attending a funeral earlier in the week, it certainly makes you think about your life and about doing something that stops you from being the perennially overweight guy. But I digress.

Apple's added a new health-sensing system with an expanded electrode surface area, more electrodes, and a better photodiode array. It's now checking your heart every five seconds, so you know how your heart varies throughout the day.
So many electrodes...

The new Readiness score also sounds like a decently simple way to measure your capacity to work out, or quite frankly, to deal with the day ahead. It's a fairly clear signal to anyone that they need to care more about themselves.
It's not quite the Apple Watch screaming "Get more sleep!" or "Work out more!" but it's going to be helpful to some of its audience.
This all plays into Apple's changes in the Health app on iPhone and iPad, with a greater use of Apple Intelligence. Though I fear many will look at Health Age with some trepidation.

I fear that if I check that figure out, I'll face questions from Apple Intelligence asking how I'm not dead yet.
Would you just stop already?

The Apple Watch Series 4, still working on my wrist. It's more scuffed now, though.

This is a problem that Apple has partially solved. With the introduction of the fitness tracking capability in the Beats Powerbeats Pro 2, it does mean I can do some workouts and exercise without the Apple Watch at all.
However, if I want to check my health from throughout the day, that's not an option. I still have to stick with the Apple Watch and live with the potential auditory distraction.
At least the Whoop-like tracker will be there for keeping tabs on my day.
It'll still be silently judging me, but that's the point.

units.text: Apple has redesigned the Apple Pay checkout flow in iOS 27 for apps and websites. The changes make it easier to switch between different payment cards and see key details about the order you’re placing.

In iOS 27, you can now swipe between payment cards right on the main Apple Pay interface. You can also tap a card to view a grid-style interface that shows all your available Apple Pay cards in one place.
Apple explains:

Apple Pay is introducing an updated design for users when they check out on the web and in apps. The design allows them to seamlessly swipe to switch cards, conveniently surfacing important information about their eligible cards in Apple Wallet — including rewards, balances, debit account balance, pay later options, and more — so they can make more informed payment decisions.
Merchants and developers have control over what appears on the Apple Pay payment sheet, depending on the exact information they need to complete your order.

The iOS 26 version of the Apple Pay checkout flow has been criticized for being unintuitive. For instance, people often tapped the wrong thing when trying to switch between payment cards. The instinct is to tap the card itself, but in iOS 26, that would take you to the address-editing interface. You’d have to tap a separate button at the bottom to actually switch to a different card. iOS 27 streamlines all of this and makes it a lot clearer.

units.text: 苹果新任首席执行官约翰·特纳斯日前向员工宣布，公司将延续多年来的感恩节特别休假传统。按照最新安排，绝大多数美国员工将在感恩节当周获得整周假期，以表彰其过去一年的工作成果和贡献。
根据曝光的内部邮件内容，特纳斯表示，公司希望通过额外休假奖励员工一年来的努力。他在邮件中提到，自己此前在纽约亲眼看到消费者体验苹果最新产品时流露出的兴奋与喜悦，无论是新一代iPhone的先进相机系统、Apple Watch的智能健康功能，还是最新AirPods带来的听觉体验，都获得了积极反响。而在他看来，这些成果离不开整个苹果团队的共同努力。
特纳斯在信中指出，过去一年是苹果取得众多重要成果的一年，而这些成果背后凝聚着各团队持续不断的投入。因此，公司认为员工理应获得充分休息和与家人团聚的时间。
按照新安排，美国大部分团队除原本的感恩节假期外，还将额外获得感恩节前的周一、周二和周三三天休假。这意味着多数符合条件的员工将实现从周一至周五的整周休息。
不过，并非所有员工都会在同一时间休假。由于业务运营需要，零售门店员工以及AppleCare客户支持团队仍需在部分时段维持服务运作。对于这些员工以及苹果海外团队，公司将允许他们在未来其他时间补休相同天数。
特纳斯同时在邮件中感谢员工在过去一年中的付出，并鼓励大家利用这段时间放松身心，陪伴家人和朋友。他表示，当前正是苹果发展历程中一个极具活力和机遇的阶段，而自己也十分期待公司未来的发展方向。
事实上，这项感恩节额外休假制度已经成为苹果内部一项延续多年的传统。
虽然外界难以确认这一做法最早是否由史蒂夫·乔布斯正式建立，但可以确认的是，Tim Cook在2011年接任苹果CEO后，于当年的首个感恩节便向员工提供了类似安排。此后多年，这项福利逐渐被固定下来，并成为苹果企业文化的一部分。
过去也曾有人建议苹果在感恩节期间保持更多零售门店营业，以抓住节日购物季带来的销售机会。尤其是在2010年代初，美国不少大型零售商会选择在感恩节当天营业，希望提前抢占黑色星期五消费热潮。
苹果也曾进行过有限尝试。例如纽约第五大道Apple Store、夏威夷威基基门店以及拉斯维加斯部分门店曾在特殊时期于感恩节开放营业。但后来苹果管理层逐渐倾向于让员工享受完整假期，并将这一理念长期保留下来。
随着约翰·特纳斯正式接掌苹果，这项广受员工欢迎的福利并未发生变化。此次决定也被视为新管理层释放的一项明确信号：即便领导层已经更替，苹果仍希望延续长期以来重视员工贡献和企业文化传承的管理传统。

units.text: After the release of Vision Pro, everyone wanted to know how long it would be before the company could release a lighter version that isn’t so bulky on your face. For the longest time, we had been looking forward to a so-called Vision Air, codenamed N100. That project was shelved last year, though the company is working on a new project with similar aspirations, per Bloomberg.

Unlike the previous N100 project, it doesn’t seem the new project, N224, is necessarily targeted at being a lower cost offering. It could instead be a successor to the current M5-based Vision Pro model, though it might still come in at a lower price while offering the flagship experience.

This new version seems relatively early in the works, with Bloomberg reporting that it could arrive between late 2028 and early 2029. That said, it isn’t quite clear what exactly Apple will be going for. The company currently has four concepts in the works.

One of the concepts is similar to the recently unveiled Meta VR glasses, which offloads the compute and battery to an external puck. Given the fact that Vision Pro already has an external battery, offloading the compute doesn’t necessarily seem like a major hurdle, though you’d need better thermals and more efficient compute to pull that off.
On the other hand, some Apple executives reportedly don’t love the idea of an external puck, and “want the company to stick with something closer to an all-in-one design.”
Design wise, Apple might get a bit more experimental compared to the current Vision Pro, with the company supposedly considering other material choices. From the Power On newsletter:

One design in testing retains the basic egg-shaped form of the current Vision Pro, but Apple is actively exploring ways to reduce its weight by experimenting with plastic, titanium, other metals and various materials. The company has also continued to explore a standalone puck that combines the computing components and battery, similar to the approach used by Meta’s recent VR Glasses.
Wrap up

Time will tell what Apple will actually end up delivering. Given the A20 Pro chip being incredibly performant at its thermal envelope, it seems highly likely that in another 2 years, we could have an A-series chip capable of running visionOS at a higher capacity than the current M5, while not needing active cooling.

I do think Apple should go all in on the Meta VR glasses idea. Even at a higher price point, I think the form factor makes a ton of sense. Apple silicon, EyeSight, and visionOS will allow the product stand out.

units.text: Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is working on a screenless fitness tracker, akin to a WHOOP or Fitbit Air. As someone who’s used the WHOOP for the past 6 months, I do think its a great concept, though there are a few things I’d like to see Apple do better.

We don’t have many details on what Apple’s screenless fitness tracker will look like, as the product is relatively early in development. At the earliest, it would debut in 2028. Bloomberg describes it as a “thin fabric band with a sensor-equipped computing module.”

Earlier this year, WHOOP and Chase had a promo where you could get a discounted or free WHOOP if you had a Sapphire card, and I took advantage of that. Since then, I’ve been a WHOOP user – though I never went all in on it.

The reasoning for that was simple: automatic workout detection will never be perfect, and I found it annoying to have to pull out my phone to log a workout, whether that be beforehand or retroactively. With the Apple Watch, you can just start the workout on the screen, and the WHOOP will sync the times from Apple Health. This was the main reason I kept wearing my Apple Watch.
For gym workouts, pulling out your phone might be fine, but for casual biking for long walks I’d rather not have to fiddle with my phone.

So, for Apple’s screenless fitness tracker, I’d love to see some sort of button and indicator LED that you can use for starting and stopping a workout. You’d still need to go on your phone later to categorize the workout, but I’d much rather do that than have to deal with it in the moment. Apple could also develop a classification model based on certain factors.
Wrap up

If Apple managed to develop a screenless fitness tracker that didn’t feel like a pain to use without a phone, I think it’d be quite compelling. The form factor has many advantages, including comfort, battery life, and the ability to wear it alongside a traditional watch.

Personally, after evaluating the WHOOP, I do think I prefer just having a smartwatch, even with the battery life disadvantages. I do understand wanting something screenless so its distraction-free, but personally I just enable Do Not Disturb on my watch.
What do you think about Apple working on a screenless fitness tracker? What pricepoint would it need to be for you to buy one? Let us know in the comments.

units.text: For the past year, we’ve been looking forward to a new iPad mini refresh, and it’s sounding like its just around the corner. A new leak last week from Aaron Perris unveiled that the product should feature an A20 Pro chip and thinner bezels, and we already know it’ll feature OLED and a water resistant design.
While those upgrades are excellent, I have one major thing I want from the next iPad mini, and it has to do with software.
After seeing the iPhone Duo, I’m amazed at how well Apple mastered the multitasking on the device. Multitasking on iPad has always felt like a mess to me, and iPhone Duo just feels elegant.

On such a small screen, having proper windowing on the iPad mini never felt appropriate. Users likely aren’t overlapping many windows on iPad mini. That’s why I want Apple to steal one nifty feature from the iPhone Duo: split screen with picture in picture.

I mean really, this is such an excellent experience. Currently, there’s no way on iPad mini to make a picture in picture window take up the entire width of the device in portrait, and even if there were, you’d either have to have it block some of your app, or manually align the sizing using windowing.

Bringing video and app split view to the iPad mini‘s display seems like a no brainer to me, especially given the fact that the iPhone Duo and iPad mini share similar aspect ratios. At least personally, I’d use an iPad mini in portrait a lot more if this feature existed.

X10 Pro Max、小米18 Pro Max和iPhone 18 Pro Max这四台热门机型拉到一起聊聊。这份长焦摄影手机排行榜不玩虚的，咱们一台一台说。 为了让大家更直观地了解这几款手机的差异，我整理了一份参数对比表： 接下来，我就和大家聊聊这几款机型的具体表现，以及它们各自适合什么样的用户。 vivo X500 Pro Max：长焦摄影手机排行榜里的“远摄课代表” 在我心里，这台机器就是冲着“拍远”两个字来的。它那颗蔡司2亿像素APO超级长焦，用的是1/1.4英寸的三星HP0大底，85mm焦段，支持3.5倍光学变焦，还带15cm长焦微距，关键是主摄和长焦都给到了CIPA7.0级防抖，手持拉到高倍率也不慌。更狠的是它还能外接400mm蔡司增距镜G2 Ultra，演唱会坐看台后排也能把舞台拍清楚，这点我是真喜欢。主摄是5000万像素的蓝图光御900，动态范围达到17EV，逆光拍人基本不用修。屏幕上了一块6.85英寸的2K144Hz直屏，京东方Q11材质，观感和触控都很顺。天玑 9600 Pro这颗2nm芯片配8000mAh蓝海电池，90W有线加40W无线，出门拍一天也顶得住。 推荐购买人群：摄影爱好者、演唱会常客、旅行拍照党，2亿像素大底长焦加上可扩展的400mm增距镜，远摄能力在四台机器里非常突出；8000mAh大电池配合防抖拉满的长焦，长时间举着拍舞台、拍风景都更省心。 OPPO Find X10 Pro Max：长焦摄影手机排行榜中的“全焦段2亿选手” OPPO这台的思路和别家不太一样，它直接把主摄、超广角、长焦三颗镜头全部做到了2亿像素，行业里这么干的目前就它一个。长焦是2亿像素、f/2.1光圈，70mm焦段拍人像特别顺手，还有CIPA7.5级防抖兜底。我个人更想夸的是它的色彩，第二代丹霞色彩还原镜头配合LUMO原生光影引擎，拍完不用调，预览啥样成片就啥样，哈苏那套“还原美”的思路确实落地了。视频方面支持全焦段8KLog录制，后期空间给得很足。配置也没短板：天玑 9600 Pro、6.78英寸明眸护眼直屏、8000mAh冰川电池加80W有线50W无线，7999元就能拿下16GB+512GB，是四台里入手门槛相对友好的一台。 推荐购买人群：拍照党、人像摄影爱好者、对色彩还原较真的用户，三颗2亿像素镜头覆盖了从超广角到长焦的全部焦段，随手一拍就是高解析力成片；哈苏色彩加全焦段8KLog，对想玩视频后期的人也很友好。 Xiaomi 18 Pro Max：长焦摄影手机排行榜上的“性能水桶机” 小米这台给我的感觉就是俩字：能堆。徕卡双2亿组合——2亿像素的光影猎人960L主摄，1/1.28英寸大底还带LOFIC高动态技术，2亿像素潜望长焦支持3.2倍光学变焦和12cm长焦微距，拍远景、拍花草细节都够用。性能是它另一张牌，第六代骁龙8超级至尊版，CPU主频冲到5GHz以上，安兔兔跑分480多万，配环形冷泵散热，打游戏长时间高负载也稳。屏幕是6.9英寸的超级像素2.0直屏，4000尼特峰值亮度，还支持硬件级智能防窥，地铁上刷手机不怕旁边人瞟。8500mAh金沙江电池在四台里容量偏大，100W有线加50W无线，回血速度也快。对了，背后那块AI百变背屏挺好玩，能当取景器也能显示外卖、打车信息。 推荐购买人群：重度手机用户、游戏玩家、喜欢尝鲜新功能的数码爱好者，旗舰级芯片加大电池保证了两三年不过时的底子；徕卡双2亿影像配合AI影像大模型，拍照和玩法都兼顾到了。 iPhone 18 Pro Max：长焦摄影手机排行榜里的“视频标杆” 苹果这台的思路还是熟悉的味道：像素不拼数量，4800万像素融合式主摄加了物理可变光圈，f/1.48到f/4.0四档可调，晚上拍照进光量明显更足；4800万像素潜望长焦支持4倍光学变焦和8倍光学品质变焦，解析力够扎实。但真正让我觉得值回票价的还是视频，4K杜比视界、前后摄像头同步双拍，加上新的Apple Reference Image验真功能，拍出来的素材专业感很足。A20 units.text: 苹果最新推出的A20 Pro芯片正在刷新外界对智能手机性能的认知。最新测试结果显示，搭载A20 Pro的iPhone 18 Pro Max已经能够通过模拟运行经典开放世界游戏《侠盗猎车手5》，并在接近桌面级显卡NVIDIA GTX 1650的性能水平下实现流畅运行。
此次测试由开发者项目Vapor完成。虽然《GTA 5》尚未正式推出iOS版本，但开发团队已经成功让游戏在iPhone 18 Pro Max上运行，并公开展示了完整基准测试数据。
根据测试结果，在1080P分辨率和DirectX 11环境下，游戏在城市驾驶场景中的平均帧率达到66FPS，在其他测试场景中的平均帧率达到80FPS。
为了保证画质和性能平衡，测试采用了高纹理质量、FXAA抗锯齿、16倍各向异性过滤、75%人口密度、50%视距缩放以及锐利阴影设定，同时关闭MSAA抗锯齿功能。
在这些参数下，A20 Pro所呈现出的《GTA 5》运行效果已经接近GTX 1650显卡在类似设置下的表现。考虑到这是一颗手机处理器，而且游戏仍运行在模拟环境中，这一成绩被认为极具突破性。
更令人关注的是功耗表现。
测试数据显示，A20 Pro在实现接近GTX 1650游戏性能的同时，性能功耗比达到后者的约11.8倍，也就是大约1180%的优势。这意味着苹果最新移动芯片能够以远低于传统桌面显卡的能耗完成相近图形计算任务。
开发者表示，目前《GTA 5》在iPhone上的运行仍属于持续开发阶段，一些兼容性问题和视觉细节尚未完全解决，因此当前成绩并非最终版本表现。但即便如此，测试结果已经证明现代手机SoC正在逐渐进入过去只有PC硬件才能达到的性能领域。
业内人士认为，苹果近年来持续强化移动端3A游戏能力是实现这一成绩的重要基础。从A17 Pro率先支持主机级游戏开始，到今天A20 Pro运行大型PC游戏，苹果正在不断推动手机游戏平台向高端化发展。

units.text: 科技行业分析机构发布最新供应链预测报告指出，苹果公司未来几年的混合现实与可穿戴设备路线图已经逐渐清晰。根据供应链掌握的最新研发进度，苹果计划在2027年正式推出其首款消费级轻量化智能眼镜产品，而备受期待的第二代升级版Apple Vision Pro头显则预计将推迟至2028年问世。
在智能眼镜产品线方面，分析报告指出，苹果的这款全新硬件将专注于全天候佩戴的轻便性与日常增强现实（AR）交互体验。与笨重的头显设备不同，该智能眼镜旨在替代部分iPhone的日常通知、实时导航及语音助手交互功能，不包含沉浸式虚拟现实屏幕，但在功耗控制、镜片光学折射率以及续航表现上实现了重大突破。此前有消息称，该项目在苹果内部经历了多次产品形态论证，最终确立了主打轻量化时尚外观与AI深度集成的路线。
与此同时，关于高端空间计算设备Apple Vision Pro的更新节奏则有所放缓。供应链供应链消息显示，由于第一代产品的市场需求相对小众且高昂的售价限制了普及速度，苹果选择将第二代Vision Pro的量产与发布时间延后至2028年。新款头显预计将在保持顶级显示规格的同时，重点解决初代产品因重量和佩戴舒适度引发的痛点，并大幅降低生产成本以拓宽目标受众群体。
行业观察人士分析认为，苹果调整硬件发布节奏反映出其在空间计算与可穿戴设备战略上的务实转向：一方面通过2027年的轻量级智能眼镜抢占规模更大的大众消费市场，另一方面为高端头显留出充足的底层芯片升级与生态内容孵化周期。这一组合拳有望在未来几年进一步巩固苹果在下一代人机交互终端领域的整体布局。

units.text: Pundits continue to hold up clear signs of restraint as failures while asking Apple to behave like Meta, OpenAI, Google, or anyone else but themselves, especially when discussing Apple Vision Pro.
If any of Apple's thousands of employees dare leave the company, or if one of hundreds of internal prototypes doesn't make it to production, you better believe punditry will be there to let us know.
The critical analysis almost always suffers from the same problem: asking Apple to chase the puck to where it is today, not where it is going.

Look, there are a dozen Steve Jobs-isms that I can throw in here that should tell you exactly how Apple operates. It is one of the most scrutinized companies on Earth, and yet, reporting in the "Power On" newsletter from Bloomberg can't help but ask Apple to change its behavior.
That Apple essence may confound analysts and pontificators, but one thing has held true in its long history: don't bet against it.
The focus of the week is on Meta's new "VR Glasses" that are neither VR nor glasses. Sure, they weigh 1/6 less and cost 1/3 the price, but they're also half the spec.

Apple Vision Pro has a weight problem, absolutely, but let us not pretend that Apple is actually okay with sacrificing fidelity and scope for that simple metric. Even this report shows the lengths of the research and prototyping Apple went through to try and get a smaller device sooner, but chose to say "no."

But of course, in light of Meta's "yes" with Meta VR Glasses, Apple's no's need to be seen as a failure. I'll let Apple's 2013 WWDC introduction video do the talking on this one (if it isn't taken down).
Subscribe to AppleInsider on YouTube
I mean, given the reporting from folks who have spent many long years in the industry, it seems they forget exactly who they are talking about.
A thousand no's

Apple has an untold number of active prototypes in development and magnitudes more in a graveyard out back. I have no doubt that Apple's secret projects division is working on everything from rollable OLED to drones.

That doesn't mean we'll ever see any of these products, nor does it mean that every abandoned prototype is a sign of failure and mismanagement. Every time a project is canceled in spite of the sunk cost, that is a victory.
But apparently three known abandoned internal prototypes are a sign of confusion, failure, and mismanagement.
N107: compute offloaded to an external product like a Mac, not as much visual fidelity, likely comparable to XReal glasses
N100: a "Vision Air" attempt at moving compute to the battery pack while maintaining the closed VR design
N109: a lighter, lower-cost version with a less powerful chip

These are likely three of dozens of prototypes being conceptualized at Apple Park. What is interesting is that instead of fast-tracking one of the other potential designs in the 28-month interval between the M2 model's reveal and the M5 model's launch, Apple stuck with what it had.
Meta VR Glasses are an example of what a compromised product might look like. Lower resolution, lower fidelity, lower field of view — clearly Apple didn't want this even if it could build it.
What's interesting is the "failure" narrative about Apple Vision Pro assumes a lot that we don't know. No one outside of Apple knows the success metric for the product or if Apple is meeting that.
Apple Car is one of Apple's biggest no's
Capturing a quarter of Meta's VR headset revenue in a single holiday quarter in spite of an entrenched market doesn't sound like a failure to me.

Also, CEO John Ternus is apparently supposed to dislike the whole project and has reportedly "put it on ice." Meanwhile, his press tours have revealed only positive talk of the product, insisting that unique use cases like surgeons using the product are why Apple is in this business.
However, the reports want us to view this as a reason to dislike Apple Vision Pro.
Life-changing medical procedures aren't enough, no. We need this thing to sell in the tens of millions to matter.
A possible yes

Even with the Apple Vision Pro team reportedly "on ice" they are busy developing a "revamped" N224 that could be the true successor to Apple Vision Pro. There are about four prototypes being tested, and one that even uses an external compute block like Meta VR Glasses.
Apple didn't pivot, it doubled down on its hardware and spec combination until technology caught up

That's how Meta apparently "beat" Apple to market with a device that doesn't launch until spring at $1,299. Early reports suggest it works fine, but the lack of light shields and more limited field of view and fidelity make it a worse experience.

But of course, Meta apparently "demonstrated" that Apple's execution was the problem all along with the Apple Vision Pro. Yes, that's definitely it, as long as you ignore the successes of the headset, how it has influenced the market, and how Apple Vision Pro was a clear template for Meta's latest hardware.

It wasn't enough that Meta basically cloned visionOS for its Meta Quest line and mixed reality prototypes. Nope, the company even hired former Apple design chief Alan Dye to help nail down that Apple look and feel.
But I'm confused. I thought we were all meant to dislike the guy for Liquid Glass, but now it's apparently Meta's victory for poaching him.
I guess as long as it's a failure for Apple, reporting will choose whatever narrative best fits that mold.
The inconsistent reporting around Apple Vision Pro has been incredible. It's dead, it's not, it's dead again, development is halted, it's going again but on life support.
Apple Vision Pro is the template spatial computing is being built on, but that's still a 'failure' apparently
Analysts and pundits need Apple Vision Pro to fail for whatever reason. That's why every product even close to AR/VR/MR has been deemed an "Apple Vision Pro killer."
Either this thing is dead and a failure, or it's one hell of a resilient product in spite of poor punditry. I think I'll go with the latter until I see the gravestone.

Apple's regular employee churn and reconfigurations internally don't show anything but business as usual. As far as AppleInsider has been able to uncover, development continues, albeit slowly, as Apple waits for technology to catch up with Apple's vision of the next-generation headset.
Remember, Apple Vision Pro's only true problems are its high starting price and lack of developer support. Everything else is just opinion and conjecture.

units.text: 9月27日消息，王自如又一次站到了舆论中心。这次不是因为ZEALER，也不是因为格力，而是一段关于iPhone 18 Pro的上手视频。9月25日晚，他发布了自己对iPhone 18 Pro系列的体验结论，开篇就给出定性：今年对于Pro来说，是一个非常典型的小年。然后是一句更直接的劝退——你最好不要换。
这不是王自如第一次发表争议观点，但这一次，他踩中了一个微妙的节点。iPhone 18 Pro系列刚开售，第三方渠道已经出现价格松动，256GB版本跌破官网价。在这个时间点上，一个曾经的数码KOL公开劝退，比任何评测都更具传播力。
劝退iPhone 18 Pro三个理由，一个结论
王自如给出的核心理由有三个：
第一，性能提升有限。A20 Pro芯片确实是近五年提升最大的一次，但他话锋一转——"提升大"和"你该首发买"是两回事。
第二，ID设计延续，外观变化不足以形成社交辨识度。
第三，售价上调，性价比进一步压缩。
这三个理由，每一个都指向同一个结论：iPhone 18 Pro不是一款"必须换"的产品。
但问题是，这些理由成立吗？
从性能维度看，A20 Pro的升级幅度确实可观。根据多家评测机构的实测数据，CPU和GPU性能相比A17 Pro有显著提升，AI算力更是翻倍。但王自如的论点并非"提升不存在"，而是"提升不构成换机理由"。对于iPhone 17 Pro用户来说，这种提升确实难以感知。日常使用的流畅度、拍照速度、游戏帧率，都不会因为换机而产生质变。
从设计维度看，iPhone 18 Pro延续了17 Pro的整体ID语言。灵动岛、直角边框、钛金属材质，这些元素没有本质变化。对于追求"让别人知道我换了新手机"的用户来说，这种设计延续确实缺乏辨识度。
从价格维度看，这是最有说服力的部分。iPhone 18 Pro系列售价上调，但第三方渠道在开售初期就出现价格松动。这种"发售价虚高、渠道价跳水"的现象，说明市场对这款产品的认可度有限。
"小年"：苹果的迭代策略，用户的换机陷阱
王自如用了一个词来概括iPhone 18 Pro——"小年"。这个词在数码圈有特定含义，指的是那些升级幅度有限、以优化和微调为主的产品迭代。
苹果的迭代策略一直存在大小年之分。大年产品通常伴随重大设计变更或技术突破，比如iPhone X的全面屏、iPhone 14 Pro的灵动岛。小年产品则更多是常规升级，比如芯片换代、摄像头微调、续航优化。
iPhone 18 Pro属于哪种？从硬件参数看，它确实有大年的底子。A20 Pro芯片、全新的影像系统、更大的电池容量。但从用户体验看，这些升级又缺乏足够的感知度。对于大多数用户来说，iPhone 17 Pro已经足够好，好到让人难以察觉18 Pro的进步。
这就是苹果迭代策略的精妙之处，也是用户的换机陷阱。通过年复一年的产品发布，苹果制造了一种"不换就落后"的焦虑。但实际情况是，智能手机的技术进步已经进入平台期，每一代产品之间的差异越来越小。
王自如的劝退，是在对抗这种焦虑。他告诉用户：你的手机还够用，不需要为了"新"而换。
渠道价格跳水，市场用脚投票
比王自如的劝退更有说服力的，是市场的反应。
iPhone 18 Pro系列开售后，第三方渠道迅速出现价格松动。256GB版本跌破官网价，部分渠道甚至直降数百元。这种现象在往年并不常见。通常iPhone新机在发售初期会维持一段时间的溢价，直到供需平衡后价格才逐渐回落。
但iPhone 18 Pro不同。它开售后即破发，说明渠道商对这款产品的信心不足。供给过剩、需求疲软，价格自然撑不住。
这种现象背后，是消费者对智能手机换机周期的重新认知。根据多家市场研究机构的数据，全球智能手机的平均换机周期已经延长到3-4年。在中国市场，这个周期甚至更长。用户不再追求每年换机，而是更加理性地评估"换机价值"。
iPhone 18 Pro的定价策略，显然没有充分考虑到这种变化。在消费者越来越精打细算的背景下，一款"提升有限、价格上调"的产品，很难获得市场的热烈响应。
动机之辩：真心劝还是博流量
每次王自如发表争议观点，总有人会质疑他的动机。这次也不例外。有人认为他是真心劝退，有人认为他是在博流量。
从视频内容看，王自如的论点有数据支撑，逻辑自洽。他不是简单地说"别买"，而是给出了具体的理由和分析。这种论证方式，至少说明他做过功课。
但另一方面，王自如确实需要流量。离开ZEALER后，他的影响力大不如前。格力事件更是让他背负了巨大的舆论压力。在这种背景下，一段"劝退iPhone"的视频，既能吸引眼球，又能塑造"敢说真话"的人设，何乐而不为？
问题的关键在于，我们是否需要纠结于他的动机。他是真心劝还是博流量，他的观点本身是否有价值，才是更重要的判断标准。
从这个角度看，王自如的劝退确实有其价值。在一个充斥着"买买买"的消费主义环境中，一个公众人物公开说"别买"，是一种稀缺的声音。即使他的动机不纯，这种声音也值得听。
写在最后
王自如的劝退，引发了一个更深层次的讨论：我们到底为什么换手机？
在过去的十年里，智能手机的换机逻辑很简单：新手机更快、更好、更酷，所以我要换。但随着技术进步放缓，这种逻辑已经不再成立。新手机确实更快，但快得有限；确实更好，但好得不多；确实更酷，但酷得平庸。
在这种背景下，换机价值需要被重新定义。不再是为了"新"而换，而是为了"需要"而换。你的手机卡了吗？电池不行了吗？存储不够了吗？如果答案是否定的，那么换机的必要性就值得怀疑。
iPhone 18 Pro的发布，提供了一个重新审视换机价值的机会。它既不是一款糟糕的产品，也不是一款必须换的产品。它只是一款"还不错但不够惊艳"的产品。对于苹果来说，这可能是一个警示；对于用户来说，这是一个重新思考消费决策的机会。
王自如的劝退，提醒了我们一件事：在消费主义的世界里，"不买"也是一种权利，甚至是一种智慧。

这种现象背后，是消费者对智能手机换机周期的重新认知。根据多家市场研究机构的数据，全球智能手机的平均换机周期已经延长到3-4年。在中国市场，这个周期甚至更长。用户不再追求每年换机，而是更加理性地评估"换机价值"。
iPhone 18 Pro的定价策略，显然没有充分考虑到这种变化。在消费者越来越精打细算的背景下，一款"提升有限、价格上调"的产品，很难获得市场的热烈响应。
iPhone 18 Pro的发布，提供了一个重新审视换机价值的机会。它既不是一款糟糕的产品，也不是一款必须换的产品。它只是一款"还不错但不够惊艳"的产品。对于苹果来说，这可能是一个警示；对于用户来说，这是一个重新思考消费决策的机会。

units.text: 快科技9月28日消息，根据用户Vapor实测分享，iPhone 18 Pro Max搭载的A20 Pro芯片在《GTA 5》测试中，城区驾驶场景平均帧率为66FPS，其他场景平均达到80FPS，整体性能追平桌面端GTX 1650，能效比更是高出1180%。
测试在1080p分辨率下运行，启用DirectX 11，纹理质量设为高，开启FXAA和16x各向异性过滤，人口密度75%，距离缩放50%，锐利阴影开启，MSAA关闭，通过模拟方式运行《GTA 5》。
Vapor表示目前仍是工作进展版本，存在一些小问题待修复，但整体表现已经可用。
A20 Pro的7核GPU是性能提升的基础，但真正让这颗2nm芯片在3A游戏负载下持续输出的，是苹果全新的WMCM定制封装。
这种封装将DRAM移到芯片侧面，给A20 Pro留出更大的散热和计算空间，配合iPhone 18 Pro Max更大的VC均热板，A20 Pro的持续性能大幅提升。
作为对比，上一代iPhone 17 Pro Max通过模拟器运行《GTA 5》时，帧率勉强超过20FPS，一年之内从20FPS跃升到80FPS，进步幅度达到四倍。
GTX 1650发布于2019年，TDP为75W，而A20 Pro在手机被动散热条件下追平了这块桌面显卡的GTA 5表现，功耗仅为后者的零头，能效优势达到1180%。
